automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public items published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to run time; exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

searched_topics: identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

routing_context.local_security_wiki: Owns AI-specific security findings, affected boundaries, mitigations, assurance implications, and incident lessons.
routing_context.upstream_ai_wiki: Owns broad AI companies, models, products, frameworks, MCP servers, developer tools, and general techniques.
routing_context.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: Owns general AI-assisted development practices, coding-agent workflows, verification patterns, adoption practices, and development governance.

collection_methods: Paced NVD CVE API keyword searches for MCP, AI, LLM, Open WebUI, Langflow, Flowise, agent, prompt, Copilot, RAG, and model over the exact 48-hour lastModified window.
Direct CVEAWG JSON lookups for selected candidate CVEs to confirm publication and update timestamps, affected versions, titles, descriptions, and primary references.
Targeted public web searches for GitHub Advisory Database, NVD, vendor advisory, and reputable security-reporting candidates.
Local topic-index and automation-memory review to avoid duplicating already-owned durable topics where possible.

qualifying_findings.title: Bifrost unauthenticated remote code execution via MCP stdio client registration
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Bifrost MCP client registration accepted stdio client command definitions through the management API; with default governance authentication disabled, a caller could register a command that the gateway executed immediately.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with upstream patch and release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: maximhq Bifrost transports before 2.1.0 on Linux and macOS; management API, MCP registration, and gateway command execution boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP gateway turns tool registration into code execution unless client registration is authenticated and constrained; this is a direct agent-tool control-plane risk.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the unauthenticated MCP stdio registration RCE and gateway control-plane lesson in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Bifrost as a broad AI gateway/product entity is upstream-owned if durable product context is needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General MCP gateway operation and deployment workflow patterns are upstream to ai-dev-wiki when not security-specific.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct CVEAWG record and upstream patch/release references are in-window.

qualifying_findings.title: LightLLM unauthenticated RCE through Config Server pickle deserialization
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: LightLLM through 1.2.0 exposed an unauthenticated Config Server WebSocket endpoint that passed the first client frame to pickle.loads(), enabling a malicious serialized payload to execute code.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with project issue and code reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ModelTC LightLLM through 1.2.0; Config Server /visual_register WebSocket endpoint.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Lightweight model-serving infrastructure is part of the AI runtime supply chain; unauthenticated deserialization on a serving control plane can compromise model hosts.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the runtime RCE and model-serving control-plane implication in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: LightLLM as a serving framework/tool entity is upstream-owned for general background.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: Model-serving deployment workflow notes route upstream only if they become general practice guidance.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: in-window CVEAWG publication includes affected version and source references.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI execute_code sandbox bypass via str.format dunder access
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: PraisonAI Agents before 1.6.59 allowed execute_code sandbox mode to assemble blocklisted dunder names at runtime and use str.format or str.format_map dotted-field access to bypass _safe_getattr.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: LLM-controlled code execution sandboxes need semantic containment, not just string blocklists, because prompt-influenced payloads can rebuild forbidden object access paths.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the sandbox bypass and prompt-to-code containment lesson in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: PraisonAI as a broad agent framework entity is upstream-owned for general product/framework context.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General multi-agent framework usage patterns route to ai-dev-wiki unless framed as a security control.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct in-window CVEAWG publication and upstream advisory references.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI file mention path traversal enables arbitrary file read
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: PraisonAI Agents before 1.6.59 accepted @file: mention values and fell back to Path(file_path) without traversal, symlink, or workspace-boundary validation.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prompt-addressable file references are an agent context-ingestion boundary; missing workspace containment can expose host files to model or tool flows.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the arbitrary-file-read and workspace-boundary lesson in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: PraisonAI framework background belongs upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General file-mention UX or context patterns belong upstream unless tied to security controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct in-window CVEAWG publication and upstream advisory references.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI code-agent tools fail open without a workspace boundary
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: PraisonAI before 4.6.59 passed workspace=None to code_read_file, code_search_replace, and code_apply_diff helper paths, so containment checks only ran when a workspace was truthy.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: PraisonAI before 4.6.59; CODE_TOOLS wrappers and workspace containment.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent code tools should fail closed when workspace roots are missing; fail-open containment lets prompt-influenced tools reach unintended files.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the code-tool fail-open boundary and mitigation implications in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent workspace workflows route upstream when not vulnerability-specific.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct in-window CVEAWG publication and upstream advisory references.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI Jobs API exposes unauthenticated agent-execution endpoints
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: PraisonAI before 4.6.58 mounted /api/v1/runs without authentication or per-job authorization, allowing network clients to submit prompts and agent configuration and inspect job data.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent job APIs are delegated-action surfaces; unauthenticated run creation can turn hosted agents into attacker-operated automation.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the unauthenticated agent-execution API issue and delegated-action implications in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General jobs API design patterns route upstream unless focused on security gates.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct in-window CVEAWG publication and upstream advisory references. The CVE affected-version text says product before 4.6.58 while the version entry displays lessThan 4.6.48; recheck during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI multiedit tool allows LLM-controlled arbitrary file read and write
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: PraisonAI before 4.6.62 passed an LLM-controlled filepath directly to multiedit file reads and writes without traversal rejection, symlink resolution, workspace boundary checks, or protected-path checks.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: PraisonAI before 4.6.62; multiedit tool filepath handling.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: LLM-directed editing tools need explicit filesystem authority boundaries; otherwise prompt influence can become arbitrary host-file modification.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the LLM-controlled file-write boundary issue in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: PraisonAI broad framework context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General code-editing workflow patterns route upstream unless tied to containment controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct in-window CVEAWG publication and upstream advisory references.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI IMAP command injection via LLM-controlled email search parameters
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: PraisonAI Agents before 1.6.59 interpolated LLM-controlled from_addr, subject, and query values directly into quoted IMAP SEARCH criteria, allowing command injection through quote, backslash, newline, or null characters.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with GitHub advisory, patch, and release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: praisonaiagents before 1.6.59; email_tools.py IMAP search construction.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Email tools are high-value agent connectors; LLM-controlled query strings must be parsed as data, not command syntax.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the connector command-injection issue and agent-email boundary in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: PraisonAI broad framework context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General connector workflow design routes upstream unless focused on injection controls.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM Langflow scanner blocklist bypass enables root code execution
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.10.0 allowed arbitrary Python code execution with root privileges by submitting components containing socket or urllib imports that bypassed an incomplete security-scanner blocklist.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with IBM advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.10.0; component scanner and Python execution boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Low-code AI workflow builders execute user-authored components; scanner blocklists are fragile when they mediate network, cloud metadata, and root-level code execution.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the Langflow code-execution scanner-bypass issue in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Langflow as a framework/product entity is upstream-owned for general context.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General low-code workflow-building practice routes upstream if separated from the vulnerability.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct in-window CVEAWG publication and IBM support reference. Ingest should recheck IBM page for remediation wording.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM Langflow MCP Tools cache isolation exposes another user's MCP context
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.11.5 allowed an authenticated attacker to access another user's MCP server context because the MCP Tools component used improper cache-key isolation.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with IBM advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.11.5; MCP Tools component cache isolation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP server context can carry delegated tool authority and sensitive connection state; per-user cache isolation is an access-control boundary.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the MCP context isolation issue in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Langflow broad framework context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General MCP development workflow notes route upstream if not security-specific.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM Langflow unauthenticated SSRF through flow components
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.10.2 was vulnerable to unauthenticated SSRF because flow components lacked URL validation, enabling unauthorized requests from the system and possible network enumeration.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with IBM advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.10.2; flow component URL validation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent workflow components often fetch external resources; missing egress and private-address controls can expose internal network surfaces.

upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Langflow broad framework context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General workflow component usage routes upstream when not security-specific.

qualifying_findings.title: Apple Intelligence security prompt bypass fixed in macOS Golden Gate 27
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Apple fixed a permissions issue in macOS Golden Gate 27 with improved state management; the CVE states that an app may have been able to bypass Apple Intelligence security prompts.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record with vendor support reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: macOS versions before Golden Gate 27; Apple Intelligence security prompt state management.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Local AI assistant prompts are permission gates; prompt-bypass bugs weaken user consent for AI-mediated actions or data access.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the AI security prompt bypass and local-assistant permission-gate implication in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Apple Intelligence as a broad product/entity is upstream-owned for general product context.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise cross-workspace credential IDOR via node-load-method
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Flowise through 3.1.3 exposed POST /api/v1/node-load-method/:name without route-level permission checks, allowing attacker-controlled node and credential inputs that could cross workspace boundaries.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record visibly updated inside the run window
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise up to and including 3.1.3; fixed in 3.1.4; node-load-method and credential workspace boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Low-code LLM builders bind credentials to nodes and workspaces; cross-workspace IDOR can leak or misuse provider and connector credentials.

upstream_routing.local_action: Keep the credential-boundary and workspace-IDOR finding in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_wiki: Flowise as a framework/product entity is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.upstream_ai_dev_wiki: General low-code LLM workflow practice routes upstream when not vulnerability-specific.
